findings.finding: The header declares only `jsonschema` and `pyyaml`. If `update_compliance.py` (or any module it imports) also relies on packages supplied only by the compliance plugin's own `pyproject.toml` (or on the plugin's project being importable/sys.path-reachable), the isolated PEP 723 env drops those — a regression not visible in the diff. The slow `--help` test only covers top-level imports, so a lazily-imported or transitive dependency would slip through.
findings.suggestion: Grep the script (and its local imports) for third-party imports and either declare them all in the header or confirm in the diff body that jsonschema/pyyaml are the only external deps.

findings.finding: The path-shape assertion (`script.parent.parent.parent.name == "shipwright-compliance"`) breaks if the compliance script is ever moved a directory level, and `Path(cmd[2])` assumes uv isn't invoked with a wrapper path that prepends arguments. Fragile, but not a current bug.
findings.suggestion: Consider asserting the path is a descendant of the plugin dir rather than an exact depth.

findings.finding: The test pins `returncode == 1` and exact substrings ("ok," / "error(s)") of the verifier's report format. If the verifier's exit code or wording changes for an empty project, this test fails spuriously even though the header behavior is fine — it couples the dependency test to unrelated output formatting.
findings.suggestion: Assert only that it ran (no `ModuleNotFoundError`, stdout non-empty, exit code in {0,1}) and leave the report-format contract to the verifier's own tests.

findings.finding: The test sets `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` to a fake key and asserts `status == "error"` with a reason other than "openai package not installed". This relies on the condenser attempting a real network call (which will fail auth) — reasonable, but the assertion passes for any error reason (e.g. a prompt-file parsing bug), so it only half-validates "the import resolved". Acceptable given the comment pointing at the unit test for the fallback, but note the coverage gap.
findings.suggestion: Optionally also assert the error reason mentions the API/provider call rather than any arbitrary error.  No security issues introduced: no secrets, no injection surface change; the fake API key in the test is deliberately non-real and scoped to a subprocess.  Overall assessment: the change is sound, matches the spec, and the tests genuinely exercise `uv run` from an unrelated cwd (not just the header text). The medium finding about whether `update_compliance.py` has undeclared third-party imports is the only thing worth verifying before merge.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
